purpose: Convert Part I NPCs from static dialogue actors into bounded, context-aware inhabitants with identity, routines, memory, goals, needs, emotions, relationships and knowledge limits while preserving film chronology and low-spec performance.
design_principles: NPC intelligence may enrich moment-to-moment play but cannot alter mandatory film outcomes.
Named story characters receive richer identity/memory than ambient populations.
Ambient populations use aggregate/archetype state rather than expensive per-instance persistence.
Dialogue must respect character knowledge and admit ignorance when knowledge is unavailable.
All gameplay-critical NPC intelligence must run fully offline with zero network/API dependency.

If a language model is ever used at runtime, it must be a local on-device model behind strict context, memory, knowledge and performance limits; cloud/remote LLM calls are not part of the game architecture.

persistent_memory.policy: Compact event IDs and relationship deltas only; no raw transcript persistence.

goals_needs_emotions.rule: Needs/emotions bias existing bounded routines; they never own quest progression.

relationships.rule: Relationship state may influence reactions/dialogue but cannot rewrite canon outcomes.

speech.rule: If speech is shipped, STT/TTS must execute locally/offline and must not become a hard gameplay dependency.

rules: A character may only answer from authored profile knowledge, completed story state and remembered events.
If the requested information is outside that knowledge envelope, the response should express uncertainty or ignorance.
Book/lore details may enrich a character only when compatible with the active film-continuity point.
Lore research is evidence for authored profile data, not direct runtime authority.

rollout.scope: One Shire archetype + named Shire residents
Merry, Pippin, Arwen, Boromir, Legolas, Gimli, Elrond, Galadriel, Haldir, Saruman

acceptance_criteria: NPC behavior changes with schedule, danger, weather and bounded internal needs.
Important named NPC memories survive save/load within configured budgets.
NPC dialogue never reveals future story knowledge.
NPCs can express ignorance when profile knowledge is absent.
Relationships and memories influence dialogue/reactions without changing required story outcomes.
Ambient simulation stays distance-throttled and low-cost.
Game remains fully functional with the network physically unavailable.
No gameplay-critical NPC path makes remote HTTP/API calls.
Any future local LLM/STT/TTS layer has a deterministic local fallback and stays within the target-device budget.
explicit_non_goals_for_current_batch: large local LLM on the 8 GB / ~2 GB VRAM target
final facial animation, final TTS voice or final lip-sync
remote/cloud STT or TTS runtime integration
API keys or internet connectivity required by the shipped game

offline_runtime_policy.rule: Disconnecting the machine from the internet must not disable NPC routines, memory, goals, emotions, relationships, dialogue, story progression, save/load, STT/TTS if those speech layers are shipped, or any other gameplay-critical feature.
